title: Add Reverse-Digit Lists Problem

content.problemStatement:
You receive two non-empty linked lists that encode non-negative integers. Each node stores one decimal digit, and the least significant digit appears first. Add the represented integers and output a newly constructed linked list in the same least-significant-digit-first order.

Neither input has a leading zero unless it represents zero itself. Each node value is in [0, 9].

For the supplied JSON interface, each list is written as an array of its node values. As an example, [2,4,3] represents 342. Aim for O(max(n, m)) time and O(1) extra space, excluding the returned list.
constraints: 1 <= number of nodes in each list <= 100
The lists represent non-negative integers without leading zeros (except the number 0 itself)
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of two lists: [l1, l2]. Example: [[2,4,3],[5,6,4]]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialized list representing the resulting linked list, e.g. [7,0,8]
notes: Return the result as a list of digits in reverse order.
Preferred approach: iterate both lists, add digits with carry, append new nodes to result list.

hidden.label: Equal length with carry at each digit
Mixed digits with repeated carry boundaries
Many zeros and single high digit
Edge: both long with sparse carries
Random mid-size with unique carry pattern
Carry produces new most significant digit

notes: All hidden test cases are concrete and use arrays of digits in least-significant-digit-first order.
The checker compares the returned list of digits (order matters).
Expected outputs must match one valid representation; inputs are constructed so exactly one valid result exists for each test case.

solution.approach: Iterative addition with carry: use a dummy head for the result list, iterate while either input list has nodes or carry is non-zero, sum corresponding digits plus carry, create a new node with sum % 10, update carry = sum // 10, advance pointers. Return dummy.next. This is a single-pass algorithm over the longer list.
solution.timeComplexity: O(max(n, m)) where n and m are the lengths of the input lists
solution.spaceComplexity: O(max(n, m) + 1) for the output list (excluding input), O(1) extra auxiliary space
notes: Do not attempt to convert the entire lists to integers when lengths approach the constraint limits; use digit-by-digit addition to avoid overflow and to meet time/space requirements.
Carefully handle carry propagation when one list is longer than the other.

bruteForce.description: Convert both lists to integers (by iterating and building the numeric value), add them, then convert the sum back into a reversed-digit list. This approach is simple but fails for very large numbers and violates the O(1) auxiliary space requirement if big-integer libraries are used.
bruteForce.complexity: Time O(n + m) for conversion plus conversion back; Space O(n + m) for big integer representation.

better.description: Simulate addition digit-by-digit using arrays or stacks: push digits of both lists into stacks, pop and add with carry to build the result. This uses O(n + m) extra space for stacks.
better.complexity: Time O(n + m); Space O(n + m).

optimal.description: Single-pass iterative addition using a dummy head and constant auxiliary space (excluding output). At each step read digits (or 0 if list exhausted), compute sum and carry, append node with sum % 10.
optimal.complexity: Time O(max(n, m)); Space O(max(n, m)) for output only.

hints: Iterate both lists simultaneously and maintain a carry variable.
Use a dummy head node to simplify result list construction.
When one list is shorter, treat missing digits as zero and continue processing until both lists and carry are exhausted.
followUps: How would you modify the solution if digits were stored most-significant-digit-first?
Can you implement the addition in-place by reusing nodes from the longer input list (if allowed)?
learningObjectives: Designing single-pass algorithms with constant auxiliary space
similarProblems: Sum of Two Integers represented as linked lists

boilerPlates.Python3:
import sys, json

class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, x=0, next=None):
        self.val = x
        self.next = next

class Solution:
    def addTwoNumbers(self, l1: ListNode, l2: ListNode) -> ListNode:
        dummy = ListNode(0)
        cur = dummy
        carry = 0
        p, q = l1, l2
        while p is not None or q is not None or carry:
            x = p.val if p else 0
            y = q.val if q else 0
            total = x + y + carry
            carry = total // 10
            cur.next = ListNode(total % 10)
            cur = cur.next
            if p: p = p.next
            if q: q = q.next
        return dummy.next

if __name__ == '__main__':
    args = json.loads(sys.stdin.readline())
    l1_vals, l2_vals = args[0], args[1]
    def build(vals):
        head = None
        cur = None
        for v in vals:
            node = ListNode(v)
            if not head:
                head = node
                cur = node
            else:
                cur.next = node
                cur = cur.next
        return head
    def to_list(node):
        out = []
        while node:
            out.append(node.val)
            node = node.next
        return out
    l1 = build(l1_vals)
    l2 = build(l2_vals)
    res = Solution().addTwoNumbers(l1, l2)
    print(json.dumps(to_list(res)))
